official.deadline_note: Applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office responsible for the applicant's country; each Representative Office publishes its own number of scholarships, selection criteria, procedure and time schedule in Chinese and the local language. The programme year runs 1 September to 31 August; the 2026 round (1 February - 31 March 2026) has closed and the next falls in early 2027.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle, in principle 1 February - 31 March, with the actual window set by each Taiwan Representative Office; the scholarship year runs 1 September to 31 August
official.status_note: The 2026 round closed; the next annual round is expected to open around 1 February 2027, with deadlines set by each Taiwan Representative Office rather than centrally.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'The MOE will pay up to NTD40,000 each semester for each recipient''s approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses. If these exceed a total amount of NTD40,000, the remaining amount must be paid to the university/college by the student.'
benefits: Living allowance: NTD 15,000 per month for Bachelor Degree, NTD 20,000 per month for Master/Doctoral Degree
MOE pays up to NTD 40,000 each semester for approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses (student pays any excess)
Scholarship period begins on September 1 and ends on August 31 of the following year; graduates unable to graduate by June can receive the scholarship until August of that year
Scholarship period should not exceed a total of five years
eligibility: International students who must be foreign nationals with a secondary school graduation diploma or post-secondary degree(s), have shown excellent academic performance, and are of good moral character
Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macao SAE students are not eligible
Scholarship duration: Bachelor Degree 4 years, Master Degree 2 years, Doctoral Degree 4 years; total period not exceeding five years
Work permit: students can apply for a working permit with maximum 20 hours per week (except summer and winter vacation), maximum validity six months per semester
requirements: All scholarship applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office
A separate application for admission to the intended university or college in Taiwan is also required, within that institution's own deadline

For applications to undertake a program not completely taught in English: a copy of the results or certificate of TOCFL at Level 3 or above must be submitted (or taken at own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival in Taiwan)
Obtain a health certificate meeting the required items (Form B)
Sign the MOE Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement; the scholarship may be suspended or revoked
documents: Academic transcripts and supporting certificates (with certified translations where required)
Health certificate meeting the required items (Form B)
selection_criteria: Selection is delegated by the MOE to the local Taiwan Representative Offices, which may work with local government agencies, universities, colleges and cultural institutions
Each Representative Office publishes the number of scholarships, selection criteria, procedure and time schedule in Chinese and the local language
coverage: Living allowance: NTD 15,000 per month (Bachelor) / NTD 20,000 per month (Master and Doctoral)
Tuition and miscellaneous expenses: up to NTD 40,000 per semester, with any excess paid by the student
No air ticket or flight allowance is provided under the MOE Scholarship
application_method: Contact the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for your country for the application form and deadline
Submit the scholarship application and required documents to that Representative Office
Apply separately for admission to the intended university or college in Taiwan within its deadline
Sign the Terms of Agreement upon selection
official.application_route: Two applications: the scholarship application to your local Taiwan Representative Office, plus a separate admission application to the intended Taiwanese university or college.
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign nationals only; mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao students are not eligible. Applicants must not already hold student status (or be registered to begin studies) at a Taiwanese university or college, must not have studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level applied for, and must not be exchange or dual/joint-degree students under a cooperation agreement. The total scholarship period cannot exceed five years, and a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship must never have been revoked. No other Taiwanese government or institutional scholarship may be held simultaneously (excluding university discounts that top up the tuition payment)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is for foreign nationals (excluding mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao)
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any degree programme at a Taiwanese university or college; a list of universities offering degree programmes taught in English is published by the programme
official.duration: 4 years for a bachelor's programme, 2 years for a master's programme, 4 years for a doctoral programme; the total scholarship period cannot exceed five years
official.description: The MOE Taiwan Scholarship pays international students a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 (bachelor's) or NTD 20,000 (master's and doctoral) and covers approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 per semester, with applications submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office and a separate university admission application required.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan))
official.english_requirement: For applications to undertake a programme not completely taught in English, a copy of the results or a certificate of TOCFL at Level 3 or above must be submitted; where the local Taiwan Representative Office does not organise TOCFL testing, applicants must take the TOCFL Level 3 test at their own expense by the end of the first semester after arriving in Taiwan and submit the results to their university/college.

travel_coverage: the official comparison table confirms the MOE Scholarship provides no air ticket (unlike the MOFA Scholarship), so no travel coverage is recorded
verification.notes: Verified the MOE Scholarship column of the official Scholarship Comparison Table on the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship website: NTD 15,000 (bachelor) and NTD 20,000 (master's/doctoral) monthly living allowances, tuition and miscellaneous expenses paid up to NTD 40,000 per semester with the student paying any excess, durations of 4/2/4 years within a five-year cap, the 1 September - 31 August scholarship year, submission to local Taiwan Representative Offices, the TOCFL Level 3 rule for programmes not taught in English, and the health certificate (Form B) requirement.

applicant_utility.summary: The MOE Taiwan Scholarship combines a modest living allowance (NTD 20,000 a month at master's or doctoral level, NTD 15,000 for bachelor's) with capped tuition support: MOE pays up to NTD 40,000 per semester of tuition and miscellaneous fees, and anything above that is yours to pay. You must run two applications in parallel - the scholarship file to your local Taiwan Representative Office and a separate admission application to the Taiwanese university - and both have to succeed. There is no flight ticket under this award (that is the MOFA scholarship), and programmes not taught in English pull in a TOCFL Level 3 requirement.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Foreign nationals (outside mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau) with strong school or university records who want an English-taught or Mandarin-capable degree in Taiwan and can absorb fees above NTD 40,000 per semester plus living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Find the Taiwan Representative Office covering your country and use its country-specific form and deadline - the central site only sets the broad February-March rhythm
Start the separate university admission application early; the university deadline, not the scholarship deadline, often binds
Book the health certificate early against the published Form B item list
If your programme is not taught in English and no local TOCFL sitting exists, plan to sit TOCFL Level 3 in Taiwan by the end of your first semester at your own expense
Check that your target programme's tuition and miscellaneous fees do not exceed NTD 40,000 per semester, or budget the gap
Confirm you hold no other Taiwanese government or institutional scholarship (university top-up discounts are the exception)
common_rejection_risks: Treating the scholarship application as sufficient without a successful university admission application
Mainland China, Hong Kong or Macao nationality or household registration, which is excluded
Prior study in Taiwan at the same degree level, or current student status at a Taiwanese institution
Missing the Representative Office's own deadline while waiting for the university result
Holding or having held a revoked Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition and miscellaneous fees above NTD 40,000 per semester, airfares (no ticket is provided), accommodation and all living costs beyond the NTD 15,000-20,000 monthly allowance.
document_audit: Transcripts and certificates in languages other than the accepted ones need certified translations
The health certificate must match the published Form B items, not a generic medical check
alerts: Do not confuse this award with the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship (NT$33,000 plus a one-way air ticket, diplomatic-ally priority) or the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (Mandarin only, no tuition component)
Recipients sign a Terms of Agreement and the scholarship can be suspended or revoked; the total period is capped at five years
Work rights are limited: 20 hours per week outside vacations, six months maximum validity per semester, under the foreign-worker employment regulations
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Scholarship file to the local Taiwan Representative Office plus a separate admission application to the university; both must succeed, then the Terms of Agreement is signed.

applicant_utility.summary: The MOFA scholarship is a living allowance with a flight attached: NT$33,000 a month for degree study (NT$28,000 for the pre-degree Mandarin LEP) plus one one-way economy ticket, and MOFA is explicit that recipients cover everything else - tuition reduction at your university is possible but discretionary, never guaranteed. In principle it goes to students from Taiwan's diplomatic partners, with special consideration for others, so applicants from non-ally countries should treat selection as competitive rather than routine. The window is 1 February - 31 March each year, so a February-March 2026 miss means waiting for the 2027 cycle.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students from Taiwan's diplomatic partners (and, with special consideration, other countries) seeking a funded degree or a funded pre-degree Mandarin year who can self-fund tuition, housing and living costs beyond the stipend and ticket.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality situation against the diplomatic-partner principle before applying, and prepare to justify 'special consideration' if you are from a non-ally country
Prepare the MOFA application form and Terms of Agreement from the official MOFA or Taiwan Scholarships portal within the 1 February - 31 March window
Ask your target university directly whether it offers MOFA recipients reduced tuition and miscellaneous fees - the reduction is discretionary per institution
Verify you have never studied in Taiwan at the same level (including LEP) you are applying for
Budget for everything beyond the stipend: tuition (unless discounted), housing, insurance and daily living costs
common_rejection_risks: Being a national of the ROC (Taiwan) or an overseas compatriot student
Prior study in Taiwan at the same degree level or LEP
Mainland China, Hong Kong or Macao nationality - not applicable
Assuming the stipend covers tuition: MOFA publishes no tuition subsidy, so an undiscounted fee schedule breaks the budget
Simultaneous exchange-student status under a university cooperation agreement while holding the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and miscellaneous fees (unless the university grants a discretionary reduction), accommodation, insurance and all living costs beyond the NT$33,000/NT$28,000 monthly stipend; only a one-way economy ticket is provided.
document_audit: Use the official MOFA application form and Terms of Agreement, plus the separate plane ticket application form for the air ticket
The health certificate must meet the published Form B items
alerts: The guidelines' 'from February 1 to March 31' carries no year - confirm the current cycle's dates on the Taiwan Scholarships site before planning
Award periods must be continuous: switching from LEP to a degree programme or stopping breaks the award, and the five-year total cap is absolute
The MOFA award is distinct from the MOE Taiwan Scholarship (tuition up to NTD 40,000/semester plus a smaller stipend but no ticket) - check which one fits your finances before choosing where to apply
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Application within the 1 February - 31 March window through the Taiwan Scholarships portal / local Taiwan Representative Office, following the MOFA programme guidelines.
